U.S. Restores Key Nuclear Weapons Manufacturing Capability After 20 Years

For the first time in 20 years, the United States can once again produce a specialized material used in U.S. nuclear weapons, marking a major step toward the modernization of the nuclear stockpile.

National Nuclear Security Administration

November 5, 2026

Estimated Read Time 

 min

The Nuclear Security Enterprise is focused on modernization under President Trump’s leadership 
WASHINGTON – 
For the first time in 20 years,

the United States can once again produce a specialized material used in U.S. nuclear weapons, marking a major step toward the modernization of the nuclear stockpile. The National Nuclear Security Administration (NNSA) has qualified the 
Y-12 National Security Complex
 to resume production of a material known as “binary” alloy, ending two decades of reliance on a limited supply of material manufactured years ago.
Binary alloy is used to manufacture radiation cases, which enclose essential components within America’s nuclear weapons. Restoring the ability to produce this material gives the United States a renewed source for maintaining and modernizing its nuclear stockpile. 
“Under the Trump Administration, NNSA is making sweeping investments to revitalize the nation’s nuclear weapons infrastructure,”
 said NNSA Administrator Brandon Williams.
 “This is not just about a warhead ingredient. This shift symbolizes our commitment to the long-term health of our weapons stockpile and the lasting security of our country.”
Experts from Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory and Los Alamos National Laboratory evaluated both the manufacturing process and the finished materials before NNSA granted approval to resume production. 
Y-12 is also working to improve practices to use weapon materials more efficiently, ensuring that adequate supplies will be available for future stockpile needs, while still meeting all Department of War warhead requirements.
